Israel shares intel on fresh Iranian plan to kill Trump, signaling escalation risk -WSJ

•	Israel shared new intelligence with the U.S. on Iran. 

•	Intel indicated a fresh Iranian plan to kill President Trump. 

•	Israeli embassy in Washington declined to comment. 

Trump’s Public Comments on Threats 

•	Speaking in Ankara, Turkey, Trump alluded to threats against his life. 

•	“They want to take out the U.S. leader—me,” he said. 

•	Said “I’m on every list… every single one of their lists.” 

•	Added he has been “a little bit lucky” so far. 

•	Trump and Netanyahu spoke Thursday, per Israeli PM’s office. 

•	Statement said they agreed to continue “coordination between the countries.” 

•	Trump updated Netanyahu on recent U.S. activity in the Gulf.

OPENAI TOP EXECUTIVE FIDJI SIMO TO RESIGN — WSJ



The head of artificial general intelligence won’t return from extended medical leave, a major leadership change as the AI giant prepares to go public



Fidji Simo, OpenAI’s No. 2 executive communicated her decision in a note to staff Thursday, saying that her medical condition had worsened and her road to recovery would be much longer than anticipated. She will become a part-time adviser to the company.

$GRAB plans a 15x expansion of Vietnam’s EV charging network

•	Grab plans to grow its Vietnam EV charging network from about 400 ports today to over 6,000 by early 2028.

•	Nearly half of the new ports will be located in Hanoi, backed by a Memorandum of Understanding signed with the city in late June.

•	The push offers a brand-neutral alternative to VinFast’s proprietary charging system.

•	Grab’s Electric Vehicle Utility feature, launched in April, already connects drivers to 400+ ports from providers like Eboost, Charge+, EV One, and ChargeLink.

•	More than 7 in 10 driver partners who try the feature return to use it again within 7 days.

Why it matters: A brand-agnostic charging network could accelerate EV adoption among ride-hail drivers in Vietnam without locking them into a single carmaker’s ecosystem.
*Japan’s producer prices picked up in June to the fastest pace since early 2023, reinforcing the case for the BOJ to keep hiking rates

BofA reiterates Buy on Meta ($META), sees ~29% upside

•	BofA Securities maintained its Buy rating and $835 price target on Meta Platforms ($META), implying roughly 29% upside from the current price of $647.80.

•	The firm highlighted Meta’s custom AI chip development and plans to expand compute capacity to 14GW across 2026 and 2027.

•	BofA estimates Meta’s cost per gigawatt at about $22 billion, well below its prior estimate of $45 billion per gigawatt.

•	The firm believes these lower infrastructure costs could give Meta ($META) more favorable economics than hyperscaler peers.

SEALSQ ($LAES) signed a $5 million commercial deal with Quobly to embed post-quantum security into Quobly’s quantum computing platforms.

•	SEALSQ ($LAES) will supply post-quantum semiconductor technologies, Root-of-Trust infrastructure, cryptography, secure identity solutions, and engineering services under the agreement.

•	The deal shifts the two companies’ relationship from strategic collaboration to commercial deployment.

•	The integration targets Quobly’s silicon-based quantum computing platforms specifically.

XPeng ($XPEV) has begun internal employee testing of its Robotaxi platform in Guangzhou.

•	The platform runs on XPeng’s self-developed Turing AI chip, VLA2.0 model, and proprietary infrastructure.

•	XPeng plans to move to trial operations and regular demonstration services in 2026, using Guangzhou as its model city.

•	The company is also exploring Robotaxi partnerships in Europe, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia.

Stifel raised its AMD ($AMD) price target to $635 from $450, maintaining a Buy rating, implying about 17% upside from the current price of $544.90.

•	Stifel views AMD’s EPYC server CPUs as a key AI winner, projecting the server CPU market to exceed $120 billion by 2030 with a 35%+ CAGR.

•	The firm cited MI450/Helios and the upcoming MI500 as key product catalysts.

•	Stifel also pointed to 6GW compute commitments from OpenAI and Meta as evidence of strong AI infrastructure demand supporting AMD’s growth.

InMode ($INMD) confirmed its Board received an unsolicited acquisition proposal from Steel Partners Holdings dated July 9, 2026.

•	A Special Committee of independent directors, along with legal and financial advisors, will review the proposal.

•	The Special Committee said it does not intend to comment further at this time.

A Financial Times investigation found OpenAI and Google supplied advanced AI services to Singapore-based subsidiaries of Alibaba, Baidu, and Tencent — Chinese tech giants flagged by the Pentagon for alleged military ties.

Legal loophole, not violation

•	The transactions don’t break US law because export controls target specific entities and locations rather than the technology itself, and Singapore isn’t a restricted jurisdiction even though the parent firms sit on the Pentagon’s 1260H blacklist.

•	Alibaba is separately challenging its blacklist designation in US court, calling it “arbitrary and capricious.”

Company positions differ sharply

•	OpenAI blocks direct access from mainland China but permits certain Chinese-owned companies to use its tools in juris…

Qatari mediators are meeting Iranian officials in Tehran to de-escalate tensions and pave the way for broader negotiations, in coordination with the US.

•	The talks aim to address implementation of the US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding (the Islamabad MoU signed electronically in June) and issues behind the recent escalation, including disputes over navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

•	This follows a spike in tensions, including an Iranian missile hitting a Qatari LNG ship in the Strait in early July, marking the biggest day of attacks since the peace deal was signed.

•	Qatar has been the lead mediator on Hormuz-related issues, having earlier sent negotiators to Tehran and Oman to push talks toward finalizing navigation and maritime-service arrangements as called for under the MoU.

$GTM: ZoomInfo launches GTM Bench to evaluate AI on sales tasks

•	ZoomInfo ($GTM) launched GTM Bench, a benchmark evaluating LLMs (large language models) and AI agents on go-to-market (GTM) (sales/marketing execution) tasks.

•	Tasks include prospecting, account scoring, and data enrichment.

•	Version 1 evaluates more than 20 GTM tasks across four systems and three AI models.

•	ZoomInfo said its own GTM.AI ranked highest in the initial benchmark.

•	Methodology, sample tasks, and grading rubrics have been published.

$CRCL: EURC hits record on-chain activity after MiCA milestone

•	Circle’s ($CRCL) euro-backed stablecoin EURC hit all-time highs across on-chain activity metrics.

•	Records came shortly after the MiCA (Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation) framework took effect.

•	Market participants required to operate under MiCA increasingly adopted the licensed euro stablecoin.

•	EURC set new activity records across its four-year history.

$AMAT: Stifel raises Applied Materials price target to $650 from $530

•	Stifel maintained its Buy rating on Applied Materials ($AMAT).

•	New price target: $650, up from $530.

•	Implies +10.42% upside vs. current price of $588.66.

•	Viewed as a high quality/lower-beta semis/tech holding.

•	Has a broader arsenal of products to address customer roadmap challenges.

SoftBank and PayPay in talks to invest in Seven & i

•	SoftBank Corp and PayPay are in talks to invest in Seven & i Holdings.

•	Bloomberg said the deal would likely total several hundred billion yen.

•	Nikkei later reported total investment could reach up to 300 billion yen ($1.85 billion).

•	Sumitomo Mitsui Card may also take a stake.

•	Seven & i has faced pressure to improve returns and focus on core convenience stores.

What SoftBank wants

•	SoftBank plans to use in-house AI to improve store management.

•	It also wants to introduce autonomous robots to cut manpower in Seven & i stores.

Cboe Global Markets expects to list options on SK Hynix’s U.S.-listed shares two business days after the stock’s trading debut.

•	SK Hynix raised $26.5 billion in the share sale and is set to make its Wall Street entry later Friday.

•	The listing would follow existing regulatory rules and the Options Listing Procedures Plan framework.

•	SK Hynix is valued at about $1.03 trillion based on its South Korea-listed shares.

•	Options would let traders hedge risk or bet on share-price moves and could lift liquidity and price discovery.

Israeli sources say the Trump administration wants Israel out of the Iran fight

•	Two Israeli sources said the Trump administration does not want Israel involved in the fighting, fearing it could lose control of the conflict.

•	One source said Netanyahu would want to join US strikes, but the US does not want Israel involved right now.

•	Israel’s defense minister said the IDF is ready to resume the war against Iran on its own if needed.

•	Israel Katz said the IDF is on high alert and prepared to carry out an independent strike to eliminate threats, even for a third time.

•	One source said the prevailing Israeli view is that Trump does not want a full-scale war and may only be willing to restore the naval blockade on Iranian ports.

Tencent in talks to buy Manus stake as Meta unwind is reversed

•	Tencent is in talks to become Manus’s largest shareholder.

•	The deal would unwind Meta’s $2 billion acquisition at the same valuation.

•	Most former investors, including Tencent, ZhenFund, HSG, and management, are discussing backing the reversal.

•	Tencent would likely be the biggest buyer but stay a minority shareholder.

•	Manus would keep operating independently from Singapore.

What changed

•	China ordered Meta to unwind the deal in April, citing investment-rule breaches.

•	Beijing sees the reversal as part of a wider push to keep AI talent and companies under domestic control.

•	Meta has already separated Manus operations and stopped data sharing, but the financial unwind is not complete.

$NVDA supplier King Yuan Electronics plans up to $1.4 billion U.S. investment

•	King Yuan Electronics plans to invest up to US$1.4 billion in the U.S.

•	The company supplies chip testing services to $NVDA.

•	The investment will fund a new U.S. facility to support growth.

•	King Yuan did not disclose the facility’s location or timeline.

•	Intended customers for the facility remain undisclosed.

$META: EU says Instagram and Facebook designs breach digital law

•	The EU Commission said Meta ($META) breached the Digital Services Act over the “addictive” design features on Instagram and Facebook.

•	The Commission cited infinite scroll, autoplay, push notifications, and personalized recommendations.

•	It said Meta did not adequately assess risks to minors and vulnerable adults.

•	Meta said, “We disagree with these preliminary findings.”

•	If confirmed, Meta could face a fine of up to 6% of annual turnover.

Why it matters: The ruling adds more regulatory pressure on Meta ($META) and could force product changes to how Instagram and Facebook keep users engaged.
